title: API Reference
markdown:
The FastAPI surface lives in `openexecutive.api.main`, which mounts one router per topic. A shared-secret middleware gates every request via an `x-api-key` header, except `/health` and the `/webhook/*` callbacks (which carry their own verification). With local login (`OE_LOCAL_LOGIN=1`, which only `make dev` sets, and only while Google sign-in is not set up) a second middleware answers 403 to any request whose raw `Host` is not `localhost`, `127.0.0.1` or `[::1]` (except a webhook that verifies its caller: Google Chat always, Telegram only with a `TELEGRAM_WEBHOOK_SECRET` Telegram can send), and to any write whose `Sec-Fetch-Site` is present and not `same-origin`/`none`. The UI signs that owner in with no password and this API usually has no secret, so without it a web page in the owner's browser could drive the API as the principal — by DNS-rebinding its own hostname to 127.0.0.1, or by posting a plain form from another site or localhost port. CORS is restricted to configured UI origins. The gate is off when `BACKEND_SHARED_SECRET` is unset — intended for local development only — so any internet-reachable deployment sets `OE_PUBLIC_DEPLOYMENT`, and `create_app()` then refuses to boot without the secret rather than serving an unauthenticated API.

Endpoints grouped by router:

| Router | Key endpoints | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `chat` | `POST /chat`, `POST /chat/stop` | SSE stream of a live Executive turn. The request body optionally carries `page_context` (route, page title, guide section id, and a form descriptor with current values) — sent only by the Ask OE side panel so the Executive can explain the current page or propose form values. When the Executive calls its `propose_form_values` tool, the stream emits a `form_patch` event (`{type, form_id, fields, rationale, iteration}`) that the panel applies into the on-screen form as highlighted suggestions; the user reviews and saves through the form's normal submit path. Each round of tool calls also emits an `activity` event (`{type, label, tool, iteration}`) naming what is running — progress only, forwarded verbatim and never persisted with the message, unlike an `action_taken` chip. A `session_id` in the body must be a chat the caller may use (the same ownership rule as `sessions`). If it isn't, the turn runs in a fresh chat instead, so nothing is written into someone else's session and the reply looks the same as for an unknown id. An unknown namespaced id (`slack:…`, `telegram:…` and so on) is ignored and a fresh chat is started, because those ids belong to the channel adapters and claiming one first would make the caller its owner. The client mints a `client_turn_id` and sends it with the turn; `POST /chat/stop` takes that id and halts the turn mid-flight, so the button is live from the moment Send is pressed rather than only once the first SSE byte arrives. A stopped turn emits a `stopped` event and then the usual `done` over the same still-open stream — never an `error` — and whatever streamed so far is persisted and flagged. The endpoint returns 404 both for an unknown id and for another caller's turn, so it cannot be used to probe which turns are live. An optional `memory_text` (1–2000 chars) is what peer memory records as the caller's words instead of `message` — the briefing handoffs send it because their seed quotes the Executive's own card; `POST /chat/upload` derives it from the typed text and filenames. Since it never reaches the transcript, the `chat_turn` audit row keeps it beside `message`. After the reply — a stopped or timed-out one too, before the `stopped` / `error` / `done` frames — a turn that looked at anything sends one `sources` event, `{type, session_id, sources: [{kind, title, url}], unavailable: [area]}`: `kind` is `company`, `knowledge`, `notion`, `research`, `document` or `web`, `url` is only ever an http(s) link or, for an earlier document, `/artifacts/<id>`, at most 12 sources (6 from the web, pages the reply cites first), and `unavailable` names parts of the analysis ("finance") whose specialist failed or said nothing every time it was asked. It is persisted with the reply as `chat_messages.sources`. A request that carries `x-caller-email` marks its turn signed in (`Session.web_caller_signed_in`), which Act as me needs on a deployment without local login. |
| `sessions` | `GET /sessions`, `GET /sessions/{id}`, `GET /sessions/{id}/messages`, `DELETE /sessions/{id}`, `POST /sessions/{id}/messages/{message_id}/feedback`, `GET /sessions/{id}/followup` | List, read and delete saved chat sessions (assistant messages carry their row `id` and any `feedback`). The list is scoped to the caller. Every per-session route checks ownership, because session ids are guessable (`slack:dm:<user id>`, `telegram:<chat id>`): only the session's owner or the principal gets through, and a legacy row with no owner is the principal's alone. Anyone else gets the same 404 as for an unknown id, so the routes can't be used to find out which chats exist. The one other way in is having started the chat in this process (matched by Person id or verified email, so it survives the caller being added to the roster), which is how a caller the roster can't resolve keeps using their own chat. That record is in memory, so after a restart such an ownerless chat is refused for reads. The principal can continue someone else's ownerless chat without becoming its owner. Deleting a session also drops its in-memory copy, so a later turn naming that id starts fresh. The feedback route records 👍/👎 (`{"feedback": "up"|"down"|null}`) on one assistant reply; only the session's own caller or the principal may rate it. The rater is stored (`feedback_by_person_id`), and a 👎 on a reply to the rater's own message triggers a working-style pass for them (paced; see attunement). The chat stream's `done` event carries `message_id` for the persisted reply. The followup route returns `{"suggestion": string|null}` — one suggested next user message, written by the utility-fast model from the last few turns, that the chat composer shows as its greyed placeholder (Tab / → or the inline chip fills it in without sending). It is null unless the session ends on a persisted assistant reply, and null (uncached) when the model fails. Same ownership check as feedback; successful suggestions are cached in-process per (session, reply id). Messages from `GET /sessions/{id}/messages` carry each assistant reply's saved `sources` (the same shape as the chat stream's `sources` event, without `type`), so a reloaded chat shows them again. |
| `today` | `GET /today`, `GET /today/activity`, `GET /today/activity/daily`, `GET /today/brief-delivery`, `GET /today/top-three`, `GET /today/weekly-review` | Morning-brief aggregation, recent-action rail, and Pulse heartbeat heatmap (per-day activity counts). `brief-delivery` returns the latest morning brief or end-of-day digest that didn't reach the owner, as `{brief, at, problem, fix, readable}` in plain language (`readable` is false when it couldn't be written, so there is nothing to read), or null — null while briefs go out, once the cause is fixed, while the scheduler is off, and for anyone but the owner (`chat._caller_is_principal_or_unclaimed`); it carries no address or channel id. `top-three` and `weekly-review` feed the solo Briefing's own cards and answer only in solo mode and only to the principal (`workflows._caller_is_the_principal`: a principal match or no caller header, never an unclaimed roster); anyone else, and team mode, get null. `top-three` returns `{items: [{key, kind, text, why, slot}]}` — the morning brief's top three from the same code (`build_top_three(principal_due_soon())`), `slot` a free block like `10:00–11:00`, `""` when none is left, null when no calendar was read — and is kept off `GET /today` because its calendar read may take up to 4 s. `weekly-review` returns the latest completed `weekly_review` run as `{run_id, completed_at, period, top_three, excerpt}` (next week's top three as plain text; `excerpt` when that list is empty), or null when none has completed. |
| `people` | `GET\|POST\|PATCH /people`, `POST /people/{id}/archive`, `GET /people/{id}/open-loops`, `POST /open-loops/{loop_id}/close`, `GET /people/{id}/outreach`, `GET\|PUT\|DELETE /people/{id}/attunement` | Roster CRUD and scope lookups. Every `Person` carries `kind` (`team` / `contact`). `GET /people` lists team members only unless `?include_contacts=true` (the People page asks for both; the department-head and workflow pickers keep the default); `POST` / `PATCH` accept `kind`, and a principal contact is a 422 either way. Adding, editing and archiving (`POST`, `PATCH`, `/archive`) are the principal's only, or anyone's while no one is principal yet so a first setup can add its owner (`chat._caller_is_principal_or_unclaimed`, the check behind `PUT /workspace`; a request with no `x-caller-email`, such as the CLI or local login, counts as the principal). Anyone else, a person editing their own row included, gets 403 before the person lookup, so it can't probe which ids exist. Contacts are private to the principal (`caller_is_principal`: the signed-in email is the principal's, or no `x-caller-email`; stricter than the owner rule above, so while no one is principal nobody is): for anyone else `include_contacts` is ignored, a contact's id is a 404 on `GET /people/{id}` and open-loops (exactly as for a missing id; `PATCH` and archive are already a 403 for them), and creating a contact or turning someone into one is a 403, even on a first setup with no principal yet. `GET /people/me` returns `{person_id, is_principal}` so the UI offers contacts to the principal only. `GET /people/by-scope/{token}` never returns a contact. Archiving a person closes their open loops. The open-loop routes list what a person owes (soonest due first) and close one (`reason`: done / not_needed / cancelled) — both the principal's or the owner's only (403 otherwise, via `people.store.is_principal_or_self`). `/outreach` returns, per kind of proactive outreach over 30 days, `sent` / `replied` / `acted` / `ignored` / `pending` (voided DMs are excluded) — same access rule, checked before the person lookup so it can't probe which ids exist. `/attunement` reads, replaces (`rules`: up to 4 strings, or omitted to only set `locked`) or resets the person's working-style rules — same access rule, 404 for an archived person; `PUT` rejects a rule that is not purely about style with 422. Archiving a person also drops their working style. |
| `departments` | `GET\|POST\|PATCH\|DELETE /departments`, `.../goals` | Department state and per-department goals. `PATCH /departments/{slug}` also takes `watched_entities` (≤50 names, `[]` clears) — the entities the research watch policy may add watches for and route to this department. A `cadences` spec that does not parse is rejected with a 422 (empty means no cadence). A new `head_person_id` must be a team member: an unknown id and one of the principal's contacts get the same name-free 422 (`person_id N is not on the team.`), so the route — open to any signed-in user — never reveals that a contact exists; an unchanged head is not re-checked. `POST .../goals` requires only `key_result`: a missing or blank `period_value` is filled with the current period for `period_type` in the user's zone (the same label `create_goal` uses), and `target` defaults to empty. `PATCH .../goals/{id}` rejects a blank `key_result` or `period_value` with a 422; `target` may be cleared. |
| `agents` | `GET /agents`, `GET /agents/models`, `GET /agents/models/options`, `PATCH /agents/{id}`, `POST /agents/{id}/test` | Specialist metadata and Council overrides. `/agents/models` is the flat model allowlist the PATCH validator uses; `/agents/models/options` returns the same ids in the same order, each tagged with `provider`, `provider_label`, `route` (`direct` / `openrouter` / `local`) and a display `label`, for the Council's Provider → Model picker. |
| `personas` | `GET\|PUT\|POST\|DELETE /personas` | Executive persona definitions. |
| `alerts` | `POST /alerts/{id}/ack`, `POST /alerts/bulk-ack`, `POST /alerts/{id}/reopen`, `POST /alerts/review` | Groom the briefing queue. `ack` (`read`/`ack`/`dismissed`, optional `mute_topic`) also teaches a watch-sourced alert's watch (`trust_score`); `bulk-ack` takes explicit `alert_ids` and/or `older_than_days` + `category` (exempt sources skipped); `reopen` is the Undo for a `resolved` / `expired` / `dismissed` alert (never `ack` or an artifact / decision row; back to `unread` with every review stamp cleared and its TTL anchor refreshed, so it is live again even if older than its TTL); `review` runs the Executive's relevance review on demand (ignores the interval; still honours `ALERT_REVIEW_ENABLED`, the per-pass caps, the single-flight lock and per-alert idempotency) and returns the move counts. `bulk-ack` caps ids at 500, needs `older_than_days >= 1`, and applies watch feedback per row; `mute_topic` must be one of the alert's tags or a scoped `external:` / `department:` pattern. Alerts still surface only through the briefing (`/today` reads the live view) — there is no list, prefs, mutes, or live-stream endpoint. |
| `artifacts` | `GET /artifacts`, `GET /artifacts/{id}`, `GET /artifacts/{id}/download?as=`, `POST /artifacts/{id}/archive`, `POST /artifacts/{id}/restore`, `DELETE /artifacts/{id}` | Browsable deliverables in any format — Markdown, HTML, Word, Excel, or a link into a connected app — with `format`, `downloads`, `external_url` and `supersedes_id` on every summary. `download` renders the file (Word/Excel built at request time from the stored text; any Markdown artifact, workflow output included, can export `?as=docx`) and is always an attachment with `nosniff` and a sandbox CSP. |
| `decisions` | `GET /decisions`, `POST /decisions/{id}/{approve,reject,cancel}`, `GET`/`PUT /decisions/classes/meeting_scheduling`, `GET /audit/reliability` | Approval-gated decision instances (e.g. calendar bookings). A proposed booking is surfaced on the briefing as a companion alert; approve/reject/cancel here also clear that alert. An approval whose caller resolves to the principal runs the booking inside `grant_contact_egress()`, so a meeting the principal proposed with a contact can be created. Such a booking's payload is marked `private`: it is proposed to the principal, left out of anyone else's `GET /decisions`, and a 404 for them on `GET /decisions/{id}` and every action route. Reviewed in the briefing — there is no separate proposals page. The class routes read and set how meetings are handled: both return `{decision_class: "meeting_scheduling", mode: "propose" \| "auto_execute"}` (default `propose`); the `PUT` body is `{mode}`, principal-only (403 otherwise, open before a principal exists — but then only `propose` can be set: `auto_execute` is a 409 until a non-archived principal is on the roster), 422 on any other mode, and a change writes a `decision_class_mode_changed` audit row. In solo mode the class mode decides a booking, and `auto_execute` applies only to a turn the principal started on a verified surface — any other turn gets a proposal. |
| `delegation` | `GET`/`PUT /delegation`, `GET`/`PUT`/`DELETE /delegation/voice`, `POST /delegation/voice/learn`, `POST /delegation/voice/signature` | Act as me — the **caller's own** delegation only; nobody sets it for anyone else. `GET /delegation` returns `{enabled, gmail: {status, message, email, connect_command}}`, where `status` is `connected`, `not_configured`, `needs_reconnect`, `mismatch`, `no_email`, `shared_mailbox` or `error`, checked live with Google on each call. `PUT` takes `{enabled}` (any other field is a 422); turning it on needs the caller's own Gmail connected, otherwise a 409 whose code says why (`gmail_not_connected`, `gmail_needs_reconnect`, `gmail_mismatch`, `no_email`, `shared_mailbox`, `gmail_error`). The voice routes show, learn (from the caller's sent mail, one pass at a time — a 409 `in_progress`, `locked`, `too_soon`, `not_enough_mail`, `no_profile` or `changed` when it was locked or edited while learning, or a Gmail code), edit and lock, and reset "How I write": a typed field that fails validation is a 422 `invalid_voice` listing each `rejected` field, and `clear_exemplars` / `clear_signature` drop those. `POST /delegation/voice/signature` reads the signature from the caller's Gmail settings again and changes nothing else (a locked profile stays locked), with the same Gmail codes as learning: a 409 when their Gmail isn't connected, Google refuses it or the check itself fails (`gmail_error`), and a 502 `gmail_error` when reading the signature fails. A caller `can_delegate` refuses — anyone but the principal, for now — gets 403 `not_available_yet`, which hides the Settings card. A request with no `x-caller-email` is a 403 `sign_in_required` unless the API runs under local login — a header-less call is not a sign-in (the header itself is trusted from whoever holds the shared secret, the UI proxy, as on every principal-only route). Every change writes a private audit row. |
| `audit` | `GET /audit/logs`, `GET /audit/logs/{id}`, `GET /audit/sessions/{id}`, `GET /audit/usage`, `POST /audit/log` | Durable audit trail of side effects. `/audit/sessions/{id}` adds a per-session token cost summary; `/audit/usage` aggregates token usage and OpenRouter cost across all sessions (totals, by day, by model, and by source — the part of the system that made the calls — including server-side web-search counts). Rows private to the principal (`private_to_principal`: a turn about their private mail, or a row naming one of their contacts on their own turn) are theirs alone: for any other caller, resolved as for `/alerts`, the list, its `total` and the usage totals leave them out, a private row's id is a 404, and a session shows only its other rows. |
| `architecture` | `GET /architecture/sections`, `.../sections/{id}` | This documentation surface. |
| `guide` | `GET /guide/sections`, `.../sections/{id}` | Plain-language user-guide content surface — mirrors `architecture` (static, version-controlled files; no LLM on the serving path). |
| `health` | `GET /health`, `GET /health/honcho` | Liveness probes (unauthenticated). |
| `setup_status` | `GET /setup/status` | Settings → Setup status: one light per part of the install — AI model, company setup, owner, the Executive's address, API protection, Gmail, your own Gmail (Act as me), Slack, Discord, Telegram, Google Chat, the scheduler, the daily brief (when and where it goes) and Honcho — as `{checked_at, checks: [{id, label, state, summary, fix, link, last_activity}]}`, where `state` is `ok`, `warn`, `error` or `off` (optional and not set up), `fix` says what to do in plain language, `link` is an in-app page that helps (`/people`, `/onboard`) and `last_activity` is the channel's latest `integration_inbound` audit time. It tests live, with at most one free read-only call per service, each bounded to 5 s: Anthropic `models.list` (so an organisation key missing `ANTHROPIC_WORKSPACE_ID` shows up), Slack `auth.test`, Telegram `getMe` and `getWebhookInfo`, Discord `users/@me` only while the bot is still connecting, and — once the owner's own Gmail credential exists — Google's token refresh and Gmail `users/me/profile`. It also reads the listeners the lifespan leaves on `app.state` (Slack's socket, the Discord bot and its task, the MCP gateway), the scheduler heartbeat and the pause switch. Sample values copied from `.env.example` are named as such without being sent anywhere. No token reaches a response or a log line: probes report a status code, a service's short error code or an exception's class name. Requests within 5 s of a run get that run's answer and concurrent requests share one run (kept per app on `app.state`), so the button can't become a stream of calls to those services. Gated like every other route; the UI adds a sign-in light of its own, from its own settings. |
| `documents` | `POST\|GET\|DELETE /documents`, `GET /documents/{filename}` | Upload, list, view extracted text, and delete indexed company docs. Upload is keyed on the filename, so re-uploading a document replaces its chunks rather than duplicating them, and `DELETE` removes the rows as well as the file. `domain` must be one of the nine specialist domains (including `sales`) or `general`; anything else is a 400 rather than a 200 that indexes where no specialist can retrieve. |
| `executive` | `GET /executive/status`, `POST /executive/pause`, `POST /executive/resume` | Operator pause switch for all autonomous work (scheduler, Gmail poller, workflow resumer); inbound chat and DMs stay live. Status returns `{paused, paused_at, paused_by, reason, held_actions, can_resume}` — `held_actions` counts due `pending` rows that fire on resume. `pause` takes an optional `reason` (≤200 chars) and is idempotent (re-pausing keeps the original start and reason); `paused_by` is the UI proxy's `x-caller-email`, else `api`. Behind the shared-secret middleware — not `SCHEDULED_ADMIN_TOKEN`, which the UI cannot send. Any caller may pause; `resume` is principal-only (`is_principal_or_self`, 403 otherwise; open while no principal is rostered; a header-less caller resolves to the principal as in `chat`), and status carries `can_resume` for the viewer so the UI hides Resume from everyone else. |
| `workspace` | `GET /workspace`, `PUT /workspace` | Solo/team mode, the user's time zone and the principal's role (`memory.workspace_settings`). Both return `{mode, timezone, effective_timezone, role_kind, role_title, reports_to, remit, measured_on}` — `timezone` is what the user set (null when unset), `effective_timezone` the zone in effect (`timezone`, else `USER_TIMEZONE`, else UTC), and each role field is null until set. `PUT` is a partial update: only the fields sent change; `mode` is `solo` or `team` (not null), `timezone` an IANA zone, or null/blank to clear it; `role_kind` is `owner`, `in_house`, `independent` or `other`, and `role_title` / `reports_to` / `remit` / `measured_on` are free text (trimmed, at most 120 / 120 / 500 / 300 characters), each null or blank to clear it; an unknown zone, a bad mode or role kind, an over-long role field or an unknown field is a 422 and changes nothing. Switching to solo cancels every pending department check-in, switching to team re-schedules them, and a new zone re-times the pending briefs and reflection; a role change has no side effects (the next turn reads it). Each change writes a `workspace_settings_changed` audit row (a role change adds `details.role_fields_changed`, the names of the fields that changed — never their text). The role is the principal's: `GET` returns it only to a caller `PUT` would accept and reads it as nulls for anyone else. `PUT` is the principal's alone (`is_principal_or_self`, 403 otherwise; a header-less caller resolves to the principal as in `chat`) and open while no principal is rostered, so first-run setup can pick a mode. Both work before onboarding — unlike `company-profile`, nothing here needs a profile. |
| `scheduled` | `GET\|DELETE` scheduled actions (`?status=…&order=asc\|desc`) | Pending and fired scheduled actions; `order` flips the `run_at` sort (asc=soonest-first for the upcoming queue, desc=most-recent-first for terminal-status history). `DELETE /scheduled/{id}` cancels a `pending` row (409 otherwise). Like pause it only stops work, so any signed-in user may — the UI proxy's `x-caller-email` is trusted when the request also carries the `BACKEND_SHARED_SECRET` `x-api-key` — as may a matching `X-Admin-Token` (`SCHEDULED_ADMIN_TOKEN`) or a loopback caller with no token set; otherwise 401 (token set) or 503. Audited as `scheduled_action_cancelled`. |
| `watchlist` | `GET\|POST\|PATCH\|DELETE /watchlist`, `POST /watchlist/{slug}/approve`, `POST /watchlist/{slug}/decline` | External-monitoring watchlist + signals. Rows carry `origin` (`manual` \| `executive` \| `research` \| `research_proposed`); `approve` turns a research suggestion (`research_proposed`, `dry_run`) into a live watch, `decline` `{reason: not_relevant \| too_noisy \| wrong_source}` removes it and records the decline (or, for `too_noisy`, keeps it live at a high floor), both 409 unless the row is a pending suggestion; `DELETE ?reason=` on a research-origin row records the decline too. |
| `workflows` | `GET /workflows`, `POST /workflows/{name}/runs`, `GET\|POST\|PUT\|DELETE /workflows/custom`, `GET\|DELETE /workflows/custom/{name}/targets`, `POST /workflows/runs/{run_id}/decision`, `GET /workflows/tools/search?q=`, `GET /workflows/tools/describe?names=` | Workflow catalog, run management, and user-created (dynamic) workflow CRUD. Custom definitions come back with a server-managed `owner_person_id` (the creator — the web caller on `POST`, set on insert only; a client-sent value is ignored), who is asked to approve a workflow's first write to a new target. `GET /workflows/custom/{name}/targets` lists the targets its tool steps may write to without asking and `DELETE …/targets?value=` forgets one. `POST /workflows/{name}/runs` is a 403 ("Only the principal can run this workflow."), audited, before any run row exists, when the workflow is one only the principal may start in the workspace's mode (`weekly_review` always, `morning_brief` in solo) and the caller is not the principal. A request with no `x-caller-email` counts as the principal; with no principal on the roster, no signed-in caller does. This governs starting a run only: `GET /workflows/runs` and `GET /workflows/runs/{run_id}` read stored runs under their existing rules. `POST /workflows/runs/{run_id}/decision` with `{decision: "approve"|"reject"}` answers a run awaiting a yes/no sign-off from the web app — 403 unless the caller is the person it waits on or the principal, 409 if it isn't awaiting or needs a written reply — through the same `apply_resolution` a chat reply uses. Custom create/update also rejects (422) any action-step tool that does not resolve, and so does `POST /workflows/custom/{name}/activate` when turning a workflow **on** — that click is the approval for a tool workflow chat saved switched off (turning off is never checked). Turning on a workflow with action steps requires the body `{is_active: true, definition}` carrying the definition the user reviewed; if the stored one differs (ignoring `is_active` and timestamps) it returns 409, and the switch itself is a compare-and-set on the validated revision (`dynamic_store.activate_if_unchanged`, keyed on `updated_at`), so a save that lands while the tool check awaits the gateway — even from another process — is a 409 too, so only what was shown gets switched on. `GET /workflows/custom` lists inactive definitions too; `GET /workflows/{name}` 404s for them. The two `tools` endpoints return `{tools: [{name, description, read_only, source}]}` for the advanced editor's tool picker and the review card; `read_only` is true only when the name says it reads (a label, not a control). The run stream adds a `progress` event (`step_id`, `summary`) while an action step uses tools. Each catalog entry (`WorkflowMeta`) carries `is_custom` and `background` (true for the system-run built-ins the UI files under “System”). The run endpoint streams SSE; its `awaiting_human` event carries `delivery` (`self` \| `sent` \| `suppressed` \| `alerted` \| `failed`) alongside `person_id` / `question` / `awaiting_until`, because the outbound guard or an unreachable approver means the question may never have been asked — a client must not render “waiting on them” for those. A paused run ends the stream with neither `done` nor `error`, so that `awaiting_human` frame carries `terminal: true` to say so explicitly, plus `resumable` — whether the run continues by itself once answered or stops at the gate. `GET /workflows/runs/{run_id}` returns the run row with the resume payload replaced by a small `resume_progress` summary (`gate_step_id`, `completed_step_ids`, or `null`): the payload holds every completed step's full text, and the run-detail page polls this endpoint while a run is unfinished. |
| `knowledge` | `/knowledge/builtin`, `/external`, `/search` | MBA knowledge base and external sources. `/search` is the introspection parallel of `retriever.retrieve` and mirrors its filters — including the `general` catch-all on the company collection — so the panel cannot report a specialist seeing nothing that it does retrieve in chat. It accepts `general` in `domain_filter` for the same reason. `/search` applies the same review gate as `retrieve()` — withheld (pending or rejected) built-in, external and failure rows are dropped, so the panel never advertises knowledge the Executive cannot use; it degrades to unfiltered rather than failing if review state is unreadable. `POST /knowledge/builtin` refuses a name already held by shipped content, and `POST|DELETE /knowledge/failures` now register and deregister for review — without that a user-authored failure case study had no review row, so no SME decision could block it. |
| `skills` | `/skills`, `/skills/search`, `/skills/{name}/restore` | Skill registry (the UI's **Playbooks**) CRUD and search. `PUT` on a built-in saves a company customization that shadows it; `DELETE` returns `{name, outcome}` — `deleted`, `reverted` (customization removed, built-in back) or `hidden` (built-in hidden for this company); `restore` un-hides; `GET /skills?include_hidden=true` lists hidden built-ins. List and detail carry `used_by` — `[{name, title, is_custom}]` of the workflows that follow the playbook (switched-off custom ones included) (`WorkflowMeta.playbooks` is the other direction). |
| `skill_drafts` | `/skill-drafts`, `/skill-drafts/{name}`, `/skill-drafts/{name}/approve` | Review queue for playbook changes the Executive proposed from chat. `GET` lists drafts (`action` create / update / delete, the proposed fields, an `id` version token, `current` — the playbook in effect now — and `followers`, the workflows that follow the name); `approve` (body `{id}`) applies exactly the reviewed version through the ordinary skills operations — 409 and the draft is kept if it was replaced since, on a conflict, or if its playbook vanished; `DELETE ?id=` discards that version only. |
| `evals` | `/evals/scenarios`, `/evals/runs` | Eval scenarios and run results. `POST /evals/runs` is a 403 when a workflow scenario names a workflow that only the principal may start in the mode it runs in (the weekly review; the morning brief in solo) and the caller is not the principal — the Jobs page's rule for starting a run; stored results are read under the existing `/evals/runs` rules. |
| `memories` | `/memories/{decisions,initiatives,advice}`, `GET /memories/people`, `GET /memories/people/{person_id}/conclusions` | Episodic-memory record management, plus the read-only peer-memory overview the Pulse People tab reads (`{status: ok|disabled|error, people: [...], conclusion_total}`; `?recent=` 1–50, default 5) and one person's full conclusion list, paged newest first (`{status, person_id, items, page, size, total, has_more}`; `?page=` ≥1, `?size=` 1–100, default 50; 404 when the person has no peer). The principal's own peer memory — drawn from all their conversations, contacts included — is shown to the principal only: anyone else's overview omits that entry (and its conclusions from `conclusion_total`), and their `/conclusions` request for the principal is a 404. |
| `review` | `/review/items`, `/review/stats`, `/review/trusted-defaults`, `POST /review/curate`, `POST /review/bulk-approve` | Knowledge review queue and annotations. Shipped knowledge registers as a trusted default (`approved` with a NULL `reviewed_at`), so the queue starts empty; `curate` (`{domain, action: start|stop}`, domain required) opts one domain in or out, and `trusted-defaults` returns domain → unreviewed count. `bulk-approve` takes a non-empty `domain`, `item_ids` (max 500) or `all_pending: true`, and 400s with no selector; it returns `{approved_count, item_ids}`. |
| `onboarding` | `/onboard/interview/start`, `/onboard/interview/message`, `/onboard/interview/draft`, `/onboard/interview/{id}`, `/onboard/interview/commit` | Conversational company setup. The `onboarding_interviewer` agent asks clarifying questions, then emits a draft profile + people + departments. **Nothing is persisted until `POST /onboard/interview/commit`** — the interview itself never writes. `start` is multipart (description + optional deck/one-pager uploads). `commit` answers 403 when the draft would make a different person the owner and the caller is not the current owner (setup demotes the old principal, and any signed-in user can open it). It also takes an optional `owner_email` — the principal's sign-in email, which the review screen pre-fills from the signed-in user — checked before anything is written (422 if it is malformed, already another person's, or would replace the principal's existing email — setup only fills in a missing one; 403 if the caller is not the owner and it is not the address they signed in with, since the roster is the sign-in allow-list) and saved on the principal's People row, so the owner's chats resolve to them from the first turn. |
| `workflow_designer` | `POST /workflows/designer/start`, `POST /workflows/designer/message`, `POST /workflows/designer/draft`, `GET /workflows/designer/{session_id}` | The conversational New workflow wizard. The `workflow_designer` agent asks clarifying questions (`phase: "question"`, with `hint` and up to four suggested `options`), then returns `phase: "draft"` with `draft.definition` (exactly the body `POST /workflows/custom` takes), `summary`, and `assumptions`; every response carries the `transcript`. **Nothing is persisted here** — sessions are in memory, and the UI saves through `POST /workflows/custom`. Errors are fixed strings (422 over the 8,000-char message cap or the transcript cap, 404 for an expired session, 409 while another turn on the same session is still running, 502/504 for model failure or timeout). Mounted ahead of the `workflows` router. |
| `onboarding` (fallback) | `/onboard/start`, `/onboard/answer`, `/onboard/status/{id}` | The original 12-step form wizard, kept as a fallback (UI at `/onboard?mode=form`) and used by the `openexecutive onboard` CLI. Its final answer saves the profile and adds people with their emails and a principal, so once there is an owner only they can send it (403, and the session rolls back so the owner can still finish it). `/onboard/start` reads the workspace mode once for the session: solo skips the Team Size, Team Members and Fractional Executives steps. Each status response's `current_step` / `total_steps` count only the steps that session asks, and `optional` says whether the current step can be skipped. |

| `alerts` (private cards) | `POST /alerts/{id}/ack`, `/reopen`, `/alerts/bulk-ack` | An alert tagged `private:principal` (see Today) is a 404 on ack and reopen for anyone but the principal, and their bulk sweep skips it. |
| `auth` | `GET /auth/allowed-emails` | Non-archived **team members** with an email, offered to the UI's sign-in gate — a contact is never on it, so adding a client to reach them by email no longer lets them sign in. The gate takes the **union** of this roster and its own `ALLOWED_EMAILS` env list, so env entries always work (and are checked first, short-circuiting the fetch) and roster entries are additive — a roster change can never revoke a configured operator. With local login (`make dev` with Google sign-in not set up — the UI then listens on 127.0.0.1 only) the UI signs in without an email, sends no `x-caller-email`, and the backend resolves the caller to the principal, as it does for the CLI. |

| `clients` | `/clients`, `/clients/generate`, `/clients/cockpit`, `/clients/save`, `/clients/{slug}/activate` | Client-company slots — multi-client mode for fractional use; create from current/blank/AI-generated intake draft (pasted notes and/or file attachments, multipart on `/clients/generate`), save-back switching, engagement metadata (PATCH), cross-client cockpit, delete. See the Client Companies section. |
